clusters.name: Search Constraint Composition Strategy
clusters.description: How meal discovery constraints are modeled and combined, especially for dietary requirements and availability. Orthogonal to UI, auth, and data-access patterns because it governs search logic semantics.

values.label: Specification-based dietary and availability filters
values.description: Represent availability and dietary needs as specifications and compose them to drive meal search filtering.

clusters.name: UI Data Update Propagation Model
clusters.description: How promotion/subscription plan updates reach user interface views in (near) real time. Orthogonal to persistence/auth because it concerns event propagation and view consistency.

values.label: Observer pattern for real-time promotion UI updates
values.description: Use Observer to notify UI components/views when promotion/subscription plan data changes.

clusters.name: User Interaction Flow Layering Pattern
clusters.description: How key user-facing interaction flows are structured (e.g., order history, promotions, subscription management). Orthogonal to event propagation and integration because it sets overall flow architecture.

relations.rationale: UI flows structured via MVC commonly benefit from Observer-driven updates for promotions/subscriptions, matching the platform’s dynamic UX needs.

values.label: MVC for core user interaction flows
values.description: Adopt MVC to organize user interactions including order history viewing, browsing promotions, and managing subscriptions.

clusters.name: Authentication Credential Storage and Access Controls
clusters.description: How authentication credentials are secured at rest and protected by authorization boundaries. Orthogonal to search, UI, and integration because it governs identity-data security controls.

values.label: Encrypted credential storage with strict access controls
values.description: Encrypt stored authentication credentials and enforce strict access controls around credential data.

clusters.name: Account Registration Workflow UX and Validation
clusters.description: How new users are onboarded via registration steps, validation, and confirmation. Orthogonal to credential storage because it defines the interaction/workflow, not data-security mechanisms.

relations.rationale: A validated registration workflow implies credential handling must comply with encryption and restricted access controls.

values.label: Validated registration with confirmation steps
values.description: Provide user-facing account creation forms with validation and explicit confirmation steps.

clusters.name: Domain Data Access Abstraction Layer
clusters.description: Where data CRUD/retrieval logic lives for core domains. Orthogonal to UI patterns and integration patterns because it defines persistence-access boundaries.

relations.rationale: Search filtering and availability checks typically rely on consistent repository-provided access to meals and orders.

values.label: Repository layer for profiles, meals, and orders
values.description: Use a repository layer to manage data access operations for user profiles, meals, and meal orders.

clusters.name: Third-Party Map Integration Interface Normalization
clusters.description: How external map providers are integrated through adapter/normalization to present a consistent interface. Orthogonal to UI and facade layering because it addresses provider heterogeneity handling.

relations.rationale: If a facade abstracts map interactions for discovery, adapters typically sit behind it to normalize provider differences.

values.label: Adapter for normalized multi-map-provider API
values.description: Integrate multiple map providers via Adapter, normalizing disparate provider interfaces into a common API.

clusters.name: Map Provider Interaction Facade for Discovery
clusters.description: How the system hides direct map-provider calls from user-facing item discovery flows. Orthogonal to integration normalization because it governs presentation-facing abstraction boundaries.

relations.rationale: A facade for discovery commonly coexists with adapter-based normalization behind the scenes to support multiple providers.

values.label: Facade layer to abstract map-provider interactions
values.description: Introduce a facade that hides direct external map provider interactions, supporting user-facing discovery such as pickup locations.

saturation_history.rationale: All open codes are already covered by existing taxonomy dimensions: (1) MVC for key user interaction flows and (2) Observer for real-time promotion/subscription UI updates map directly to dimensions 3 and 2. (3) Adapter-based normalization for multi–map-provider integration and (4) a Facade layer abstracting map-provider interactions are covered by dimensions 7 and 8. (5) Encrypted credential storage with strict access controls matches dimension 4’s value. (6) Defining a repository layer for user profiles, meals, and meal orders and (7) centralizing data-access operations behind a repository abstraction are covered by dimension 6. (8) Meal search filtering using a specification pattern for availability and dietary needs is covered by dimension 1.

All open codes are already covered by existing taxonomy dimensions: (1) "Use MVC to manage ghost-kitchen web UI flows" matches Dimension 3 (User Interaction Flow Layering Pattern) value 3.1. (2) "Use Strategy pattern to swap map providers and search algorithms" matches Dimension 9 (Pluggable Strategy Selection for Search and Mapping) value 9.1. (3) "Standard credential verification authentication" matches Dimension 4 (Authentication Credential Storage and Access Controls) value 4.2. (4) "Repository pattern used to abstract data access" matches Dimension 6 (Domain Data Access Abstraction Layer) values 6.1/6.2. (5) "Repositories defined for orders, promotions, and subscriptions" is specifically aligned with Dimension 6 value 6.2. Therefore, no uncovered concepts appear in this minibatch.
